picks.title: Accuracy of a respiratory assessment chatbot in a nationwide messaging system for layperson diagnosis and triage: a randomized preregistered study
picks.excerpt: In a preregistered randomized study of 2,400 laypeople, a GPT-4o-based chatbot inside WeChat improved accuracy in diagnosing and triaging respiratory conditions across 88 clinical vignettes.
picks.rationale: Preregistered randomized study of 2,400 laypeople showing that a GPT-4o chatbot inside WeChat improves patients' own respiratory diagnosis and triage. This is patient-facing evidence at national-platform scale.

picks.title: An open vision-language model for diverse medical applications
picks.excerpt: MedGemma, open medical vision-language models built on Gemma 3, are evaluated across imaging domains and clinical text tasks, outperforming similarly sized generative models.
picks.rationale: Peer-reviewed Nature Medicine evaluation of MedGemma, an open medical VLM, on clinical imaging and text tasks. Health systems can build on it without a closed vendor.

picks.title: Governments selling patient data are “betraying” their people, says AI expert
picks.excerpt: HealthAI CEO Ricardo Baptista Leite urged governments not to buy or sell patient data for AI, warning of a power imbalance with AI companies, as pressure mounts on NHS England over its Palantir data contract.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool: BMJ news on patient-data governance for health AI, set against the NHS England Palantir contract. Aimed at regulators and health systems.

picks.title: Claude analyzed my genome in 30 minutes. Now we need standards for the results
picks.excerpt: Stanford cardiologist-geneticist Euan Ashley describes an LLM interpreting his whole genome in 30 minutes for about $5 and argues clinical genomics needs validation standards before patients rely on such AI reads.
picks.rationale: A leading clinical geneticist reports a $5, 30-minute LLM whole-genome read and calls for validation standards before patients rely on such results.

picks.title: Data privacy concerns could hold patients back from using AI
picks.excerpt: A patient survey finds growing concern about how health data is handled by AI tools, which could limit uptake of AI in care even as use in daily life rises.
picks.rationale: New patient-survey data showing that privacy worries may cap AI uptake in care. Useful demand-side evidence for providers rolling out AI tools.

alternates.title: Weekly Rundown: Nextech taps Assort Health, EliseAI for agentic AI; Elsevier rolls out clinical AI tool for nurses
alternates.excerpt: Health AI briefs for Oct. 5-9, including Elsevier's clinical AI tool for nurses and agentic AI deployments in specialty practices.
alternates.rationale: Roundup with a few concrete clinical deployments (Elsevier nurse tool). A mixed digest, so it is held as an alternate.

alternates.title: AI Can Flag Cognitive Decline Earlier — Health Systems Still Own What Happens Next
alternates.excerpt: AI that flags early cognitive decline in the EHR creates a clinical duty to act; health systems must define follow-up pathways, referrals and accountability once the alert fires.
alternates.rationale: Opinion on the clinical follow-up duty created by EHR cognitive-decline alerts. Relevant, but it is commentary.

dedup.note: Dropped 3 of 10 candidates as already-published stories. (1) STAT Clairity DTC breast-risk piece is a likely-repeat of the 10-08 AuntMinnie 'Clairity expands access via Everlywell' story: same Everlywell launch, and no new release. (2) STAT 'Utah sandbox on collision course with FDA' is analysis of the Utah AI pilots published 10-07 (Healthcare Dive) and reports no new decision. (3) MedCity Teladoc contactless vitals/ambient scribe is the same launch as the 10-08 Healthcare Dive 'Teladoc unveils remote monitoring, ambient AI features'. No clusters were in the pool. The 5 picks were checked by content against the 30-day history_digest and none repeats a published story. MedGemma (Nature Medicine) is distinct from the published GPT-5 multimodal-diagnosis npj paper, and the WeChat respiratory triage RCT is distinct from the JAMA AYA cancer-chatbot RCT. Alternates are the Fierce weekly rundown (mixed digest) and the MedCity cognitive-decline opinion. Only 2 alternates survive, so the pool is exhausted. Diversity: nature.com 2, bmj 1, statnews 1, healthcaredive 1, for 4 distinct outlets. No pick touches biosecurity or gain-of-function.
